http_api.ownerSymbol: UiRuntime server semantic GET/SSE and observation GET routes
http_api.contract: The observation route parses optionalI2ReadScope, the scope subtree, node selection and decodeTaskAgentActivitySelectionQuery, then calls UiRuntimeService.scopedObservation.

load_task_truth.contract: The shared resolver selects the serve-bound live source or the declared project/mode durable inventory. Foreign admissions come from that inventory, not the serve-bound requirementAdmissions map. The same selected task scope supplies already owner-decoded native allocation, active-turn, resumed-segment, child invocation and delivery, review, and Planner records. Those typed facts are the actual-execution source; assignment-graph fact replay is not required. For a valid bound live read, App overlays only a captured pending Runtime publication state onto the authoritative same-binding durable projection; successful durable commits, output text and publicCommitWatermark remain the durable values, and no uncommitted text is exposed. A read failure retains the current confirmed commits and watermark as unknown. Foreign durable reads remain durable reads and do not borrow serve-bound live publication. Both semantic builders copy a defined snapshot publicOutput.publicCommitWatermark as the exact separate committed-output boundary; an absent value stays omitted. Missing or unavailable sources remain explicit.

project_semantic_views.ownerSymbol: selectTaskAgentActivity and the Runtime pure actual-execution selector boundary
project_semantic_views.contract: The Runtime pure selector classifies the same selected task scope's typed native records without stores, logs, Manager creation, acquire, rebind, or writes. Existing RuntimeAgentActivityProjection.actualExecutionGraph then carries the contracts source through packages/ui/projection/actual-execution-graph.ts. Guidance, current plan, and recorded instances stay distinct; exact missing relations remain ungrouped or unavailable.

project_status_and_actions.contract: UiRuntimeService builds node facts before this projection. task.output is projected only from authoritative committed public publication; missing publication is explicit and raw execution evidence is not presented as final output.

browser_view.ownerSymbol: mountSemanticObservationPanel + readSerial/streamRevision guards, closeStream/dispose lifecycle, createRuntimeReadPublication freeze/snapshot publication, createDisplayPreferenceController subscribe/dispose, and mountSemanticObservation view callbacks; task-dashboard.js/observation.js pagehide ownership
browser_view.contract: The UI-owned api.observation fifth parameter carries the complete taskScope projectKey/mode. The existing scope query remains the observation subtree and node remains the selected node; the agent query keeps the existing decoder. Both formal pages consume the same agentActivity read and actualExecutionGraph carrier without a second fetch. Presentation keeps guidance, current plan, and actual-recorded instances separate; technical IDs and commit refs stay in detail, while unavailable and ungrouped records remain visible. The shared browser projection preserves each published coverage issue's readable reason; its scope, sourceRef, and optional eventRef remain checkable in the existing read-only evidence details, and the gap never rebuilds pairing or control state. Browser modules are owner-local: runtime-api.js freezes and publishes one content reference per scope/revision; runtime-shell.js subscribes to display preferences, retains the semantic panel across renders, guards GET/SSE with read serial and stream revision, marks disconnects stale, and disposes the stream; semantic-observation.js emits view callbacks only; task-dashboard.js and observation.js dispose resources on pagehide. Task Dashboard and Pipeline Observation are the delivered preference surfaces. Other shell pages deliberately omit it. This does not establish a global event bus or a native cross-process Arc.
